When was the North South Foundation incorporated?
North South Foundation was incorporated in 1989 as a not-for-profit entity in Illinois. It was granted tax-exempt status by the IRS under the 501(c)(3) program. Its federal tax ID is 36-3659998.
When did the scholarship program start?
The program started in 1989 with one scholarship.
Who administers the program in India?

North South Foundation has chapters in several states. Each chapter is run by a group of dedicated and committed volunteers who manage the process beginning with publicity to screening and awarding scholarships. Each team takes total responsibility.
Who can participate in NorthSouth programs?
We welcome all young learners to join us! Our programs are open to all. There may be age requirements for specific programs – please check out program details for participation.

North South Foundation (NorthSouth) provides scholarships to undergraduate students entering into 3-year polytechnic (diploma in engineering), Degree in Engineering (1st year & Lateral Entry in 2nd year from Diploma), MBBS, BDS, B.Pharma, Diploma in Agriculture, BSc (Ag), BSc (Nursing) and BA.BEd/B.Sc.BEd (Limited to Regional Institutes of Education of NCERT Ajmer, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Mysore and Shillong), based on merit and financial need. The scholarship process begins at the chapter level in India with an announcement by the India Chapter Coordinator (ICC). Each India chapter has a volunteer who acts as the ICC, who is responsible for all activities of the chapter – from forming the selection committee, reviewing applications, interviewing applicants and giving the scholarships cheques at an awards ceremony. Volunteers who live in USA and are closely associated with a chapter in India act as liaisons. The scholarship process is detailed below.
India Chapter announces the scholarship call through the Chapter Coordinator (ICC).
Students register on the North South Foundation Portal and submit their online applications between.
The India Chapter Coordinator (ICC) screens all received applications.
ICC shortlists candidates and arranges interviews for them.
After interviews, ICC recommends candidates for further processing.
ICC prepares hard copies of the recommended applications.
These are sent to North South Foundation Hyderabad for record and further review.
The National Coordinator (NC) reviews applications received from ICCs.
After review, NC consolidates the data and prepares it in Excel format.
The reviewed list is then forwarded to the US Team for final approval.
The US Team reviews and approves the recommended list.
The final approved list is shared with the Accounts Team.
Online disbursements are made directly to students bank accounts.
Alongside fresh applications, renewal applications (for continuing scholars) are also processed following a similar workflow.

Ms. Modi has been chosen for the fellowship for bringing creative elements to NorthSouth coaching. She is not only one of the first coaches to incorporate interactive exercises such as Kahoots and Gimkits into NorthSouth coaching but also the only coach to have taught the classes every year since the inception of NorthSouth Spelling bee coaching program in 2020. Naysa is very compassionate and ensures that every child is learning in her class, and sets an exemplary example for all of us to follow in doing so. Ms. Modi has played an integral role in revising and reformatting the coaching materials consistently by observing and assimilating feedback from her class students, parents and other coaches.

The objectives of this fellowship for Naysa Modi are to increase adoption of NorthSouth Spelling online application by adding more quizzes and content to the website. She will also deliver a plan for asynchronous spelling classes by the end of her fellowship. She will be mentored by Mr. Narayana Janga, National Learning Journey Executive Officer, after school foundational and advanced learning programs for NorthSouth foundation.Mr. Janga has created the original Spelling Bee coaching materials for NorthSouth. He also designed and developed the modern NorthSooth Spelling and Vocabulary Bee Cloud and mobile applications.

Samvith loves to go biking with his friends in his community, but noticed that there weren’t enough bike racks in their neighborhood. He worked with local government, businesses, and neighborhood biking groups to understand the logistics and fundraising required to support this initiative.

Since his first year as a Changemaker, Samvith has installed a bike rack in his community, learned how to adapt to setbacks during the process, and is in the process of installing more racks across his community! Based on his own experiences and learnings, he advises others changemakers to understand that there will definitely be many challenges and rejections along the journey. But it is important to not take those to heart and continue to be
committed and passionate about your cause. Through perseverance and determination, you will eventually find success!

While in India, Himanshu observed that there were many street vendors, who would sell items like balloons, magnets, and flowers. Curious about this issue, he interviewed some street vendors and learned that these kids sell small items in large cities in order to financially support their families. His research revealed that 6 million children in India were out of school.

Himanshu created an Instagram page, @littlestepsforward.ycj, to create awareness about the issue. To raise funds, he also hosted a virtual Rubik’s Cube workshop. Along with the workshop and the GoFundMe Page, he raised over $300. These funds were donated to the Shifting Orbits Foundation to sponsor a street vendor’s education for a year!
After connecting with education leaders and community service groups in her neighborhood, Koyal wanted to increase access to school supplies for students who may not be able to afford them.

The collected materials were provided to her school’s leadership team to distribute to students in need.
